en.title: Next James Bond Contenders Revealed: Who Will Wear the Tux?
en.summary: The search for the next James Bond is heating up, with a shortlist of talented actors reportedly undergoing screen tests. Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the iconic spy's next outing, bringing a fresh vision to the legendary franchise.
en.body:
The rumour mill for the next James Bond is churning with more intensity than a shaken-not-stirred martini. With **Denis Villeneuve**, the visionary director behind *Arrival* and *Dune*, officially attached to helm the next 007 film, the focus has shifted to who will step into the impeccably tailored suits of the world's most famous secret agent. Amazon MGM Studios is reportedly holding screen tests this September, and a list of exciting contenders has emerged.

According to reports, the actors being considered include **Jack Barton** (*Heartstopper*), **Jacob Elordi** (*Euphoria*), **Paul Mescal** (*Gladiator II*), **Callum Turner** (*One Night Only*, *Neuromancer*), **Jack Lowden** (*Slow Horses*), and **Harris Dickinson** (*Triangle of Sadness*). While this initial group is already generating considerable buzz among fans, further reporting suggests that four names are being more seriously evaluated. These include Barton, Lowden, Turner, and a new contender: **Jack O’Connell**, known for his compelling performances in *Sinners* and *28 Years Later*. The stakes are incredibly high, as whoever is chosen will follow in the footsteps of Daniel Craig and attempt to redefine the character for a modern audience while honouring the franchise's rich legacy.

## The Talent Behind the Licence to Kill

The selection of the next Bond is a monumental decision that reverberates through the global fanbase. For years, fans have debated who possesses the right blend of charisma, gravitas, and physical prowess to embody 007. The reported shortlist offers a tantalizing mix of established stars and rising talents, each bringing their unique acting chops to the table. **Paul Mescal**, fresh off *Gladiator II*, has proven his ability to handle intense dramatic roles, while **Jacob Elordi** has captivated audiences with his magnetic screen presence in *Euphoria*. **Jack Lowden** has consistently impressed with his nuanced performances in *Slow Horses*, hinting at a Bond who could be both shrewd and formidable. The inclusion of **Jack O’Connell** adds another layer of intrigue, as he brings a raw intensity that could offer a different interpretation of the iconic spy. The involvement of **Denis Villeneuve** as director, a filmmaker renowned for his atmospheric storytelling and meticulous craft, suggests an ambitious and possibly darker take on the franchise. He has expressed his deep connection to the series, stating, "Some of my earliest movie-going memories are connected to 007... To me, he’s sacred territory." This reverence, combined with the script being penned by **Steven Knight**, the creative force behind *Peaky Blinders*, signals a commitment to a high-quality, character-driven narrative.

## What This Means for the Future of Bond

This extensive casting process underscores the significance of the next James Bond film. It's not just about finding an actor; it's about charting the course for one of cinema's most enduring franchises. The choice will undoubtedly shape discussions about Bond's evolution – will he be a more vulnerable operative, a master strategist, or a blend of all his classic traits? The fan community is abuzz with speculation, dissecting each actor's past roles and imagining their potential as 007. This period of anticipation is as much a part of the Bond experience as the films themselves, a testament to the character's enduring appeal and the passionate global audience that eagerly awaits his next mission.

## What's Next

While screen tests are reportedly underway, official confirmation of the next James Bond is still pending. Fans should stay tuned for further announcements regarding casting and production timelines as this highly anticipated chapter in the 007 saga unfolds.

According to Page Six , the studio is holding screen tests for the following actors sometime in September: Jack Barton ( Heartstopper ), Jacob Elordi ( Euphoria ), Paul Mescal ( Gladiator II ), Callum Turner ( One Night Only, Neuromancer ), Jack Lowden ( Slow Horses ), and Harris Dickinson ( Triangle of Sadness ). The Playlist said their reporting backs up this list, but that four are being more seriously considered than others: Barton, Lowden, Turner, and a fourth not on the Page Six list. That contender, Jack O’Connell, is familiar to you if you’ve seen Sinners or 28 Years Later . The decision on who will take up the super spy mantle after Daniel Craig, however, is still unclear at this point. Will one of these actors take on the iconic role? Or will someone else not on this list secure the spot? What we do know about the next movie, however, is that along with Villeneuve directing, Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight will be writing the script. Villeneuve has also been eager to helm a Bond film for years. “Some of my earliest movie-going memories are connected to 007,” he said in a statement when Amazon MGM announced his attachment to the franchise. “I grew up watching James Bond films with my father, ever since Dr. No with Sean Connery. I’m a die-hard Bond fan. To me, he’s sacred territory. I intend to honor the tradition and open the path for many new missions to come. This is a massive responsibility, but also, incredibly exciting for me and a huge honor.” No news on when we’ll finally learn who the next Bond will be, or when the film will go into production.
